conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I’m Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you during your stay. Can you tell me what brought you in today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I’ve been having this sore on my left foot that won’t heal. It started after I hit my toe in the shower about a month ago.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And what happened after you hit it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It turned purple, and then my toenail fell off. It bleeds sometimes. I didn’t feel much pain because of my neuropathy, but my podiatrist said it looked bad and sent me here.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. Given your history of diabetes and kidney disease, foot ulcers can be serious. We’ll need to check the blood flow to your leg and treat any infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need surgery?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not yet. Tomorrow, you’ll have a test called an angiogram to look at the blood vessels in your leg. After that, the vascular surgeon will decide if you need a procedure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I’m on dialysis too—will that affect anything?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll coordinate your dialysis. You’re scheduled for it the day after your angiogram. We’ll also monitor your kidney function closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my heart? I have a mechanical valve and take warfarin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We know about that. We’ll start a heparin drip to keep your blood thin while we adjust your warfarin. Your INR will be checked daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I don’t want another clot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll make sure you’re protected. For now, we’ll admit you, start IV antibiotics, and get some tests done.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We just got your chest X-ray back. It shows mild fluid in your lungs, but it’s stable. Your dialysis catheter and heart device are in good position.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that why I sometimes feel short of breath?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly. Your heart isn’t pumping as strongly as it should, so fluid can build up. We’ll manage that with your dialysis and medications.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Today is your angiogram. You’ll be taken shortly. Any questions before you go?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will it hurt?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll be given sedation. You might feel some pressure, but not sharp pain. The team will use ultrasound to guide the catheter in your groin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I trust you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The angiogram is done. It went well. There’s a severe blockage in the artery of your left leg, which explains the poor healing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need surgery then?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the vascular surgeon recommends a left femoral endarterectomy. It’s scheduled for next week. You’ll be readmitted two days before to start heparin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the infection?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re continuing IV vancomycin. The urine culture showed contamination, so we’re focusing on the foot. Podiatry saw you and agreed to keep the offloading dressing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t want to lose my toe.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re doing everything to save it. Good blood flow after surgery and antibiotics should help it heal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re due for dialysis today. How are you feeling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. My foot feels the same. The groin site is a little sore.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s normal. We’ll keep an eye on it. Your labs show your INR is improving—now at 2.8. We’ll stop the heparin soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your INR is now 3.1—perfect. We’ve stopped the heparin drip. You can stay on warfarin safely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. Can I eat regular food now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’re on a regular diet. We’ll keep monitoring your potassium and phosphorus due to your kidney disease.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We got the foot X-ray back. No signs of bone infection, which is good. But there are changes from neuropathy and old fractures.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So no osteomyelitis?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not on the X-ray. If there’s still concern later, we might do an MRI, but for now, we’ll treat it as a soft tissue infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. Afebrile, pain controlled, eating and walking. We’re planning for discharge tomorrow if all stays stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m ready to go home. What about the vancomycin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll get IV vancomycin on dialysis days until your follow-up. We’ve sent the prescription to your dialysis center.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my foot dressing?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Keep the offloading pad on. Change the outer wrap if it gets dirty. See your podiatrist soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All your labs are stable. We’re comfortable discharging you tomorrow morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What should I watch for at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call if you have fever, increased redness or drainage from the foot, or numbness or coldness in your leg. Also, watch the groin site for bleeding.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And if the groin bleeds a lot?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Lie down, keep your leg straight, and press firmly for 10 minutes. If it doesn’t stop, go to the ER.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—you’re cleared to go home today. We’ll review your discharge instructions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I feel much better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Continue all your usual meds except we’ve added IV vancomycin on dialysis days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And aspirin—discharge says 325 mg, but I was on 81 mg.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good catch. For now, stay on 81 mg unless your surgeon says otherwise. I’ll correct that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You can walk, shower, and do light activity. No heavy lifting for a week. And don’t drive while on pain meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll have help at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. Follow up with Dr. Lee for your endarterectomy. We’ll admit you two days before to start heparin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll mark it on my calendar.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—elevate your leg when sitting to reduce swelling.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll use pillows like last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. You’ve done well. We’ll see you soon for surgery.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The discharge papers are ready. You can leave once transport arrives.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I appreciate everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’ll see you next week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Remember, call if you have any concerns before your surgery.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will, I promise.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your dialysis center has your vancomycin order. They’ll give it on your next session.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I go Tuesday.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. That’s when the antibiotic is due.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve made great progress. Keep up the good work.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re very welcome. Have a safe trip home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll see you soon for your surgery.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Looking forward to it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take it easy until then.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Rest and eat well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll try.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done great. We’re proud of your progress.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. That means a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. See you next week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: See you then.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care.
